cues.text: Many orders have different kinds of clothes. The order you pack them in keeps everything neat and wrinkle free.
Think back to front. Heavy and long things go on first, in the back. Light and delicate things go on last, in the front.
One. Coats first, in the back. They are the heaviest.
Two. Dresses and long pieces next, so they hang straight and do not get folded at the bottom.
Five. Shirts, all together, facing the same way.
Six. Silk and delicate pieces last, in the front, so nothing heavy presses on them.
Folded things, like sweaters and boxed shirts, go in their own box or bag. Never put them under hanging clothes.
Comforters and blankets get their own bag.
Ties and scarves go on a hanger, never loose in the bag, so they do not get lost.
Before it goes on the rack: all hanger hooks face the same way, the piece count matches the ticket, and the ticket is on the outside.
